target_subject: a stylized human head and upper torso split vertically into two color zones

scene: A frontal view of a bald human head and neck, bisected vertically down the midline with left side in reddish-orange and right side in yellow-orange.
A white infinity symbol is positioned on the forehead, spanning both color zones.
A small black silhouette of a running figure appears atop the right loop of the infinity symbol.
action: The eyes are closed on both sides of the face, with eyelids rendered as simple curved lines.
The mouth is closed and neutral, with a slight asymmetry: the left side curves downward, the right side upward.
The running figure is depicted mid-stride, oriented leftward along the curve of the infinity symbol.
rationale: The vertical color split suggests intentional duality or contrast, though no explicit boundary marker (e.g., line) is present—only hue transition.
The infinity symbol’s placement on the forehead implies conceptual association with thought or cognition, but no textual label confirms this.
The running figure’s scale relative to the head indicates symbolic rather than literal representation; its posture is dynamic but static in the image.
object: The head has no hair, visible ears on both sides, and a smooth contour without facial hair or wrinkles.
The left half of the face features a red-pigmented eye region and a slightly downturned mouth corner.
The right half of the face features a yellow-pigmented eye region and a slightly upturned mouth corner.
A white, continuous-loop infinity symbol overlays the forehead, intersecting the vertical color divide.
A black, silhouetted human figure in running pose is placed on the upper-right arc of the infinity symbol, facing left.

symbolic_mapping: color split → dual aspects of self
infinity symbol → endless cycle or continuity
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The image may represent the coexistence of contrasting self-perceptions within a single consciousness, where the infinite loop suggests cyclical recurrence of identity states over time.
alternative_interpretations: It could be a graphic design motif for balance or symmetry, with no intended philosophical meaning.
limitations: No text or contextual cues confirm intentional symbolism; color division alone does not specify which traits are assigned to each side.

forehead → locus of intention or mind
